synopsis: The recommended test space combines an operating-domain taxonomy, a traceable catalog ensuring known fatal-accident patterns are tested, and parameterized scenario families with probability distributions; ISO 21815 and EMESRT PR-5A provide off-road anchors rather than a passenger-car library copied directly into mining or construction [f119, f6641, f1527]. Most platforms have at least 10 critical operating scenarios, but EMESRT counts remain inconsistent: a 2019 trade article reports 24 scenarios, while the 2024 Activity Report counts 17 surface storyboards published in 2019 [f17, f4079]. Scenario count is not coverage, and coverage is separate from model credibility: the plan should prioritize accident-informed cases, expose uncovered cells, and make direct statistical claims for safety-critical classes rather than rely on a full Cartesian matrix or an aggregate coverage score [f10506, f8210, f10622, f9880, f5470]. A programme starting in October 2026 can realistically have its operating-domain definition and scenario catalog working by mid-2027, with scenario development and model preparation undertaken before prototype arrival [f63, f5615]. The manufacturer should retain ownership of the catalog, operating domain, acceptance criteria and correlation data, and provide an assessor-quality catalog traced to hazards, EMESRT and ISO 21815 [f8797, f8030]. A complete scenario spreadsheet is not physical safety evidence: physical performance and false-positive tests should remain for each scenario class, alongside assessor-selected end-to-end confirmation including at least one run per EMESRT family [f656, f7884, f7887].
